paragraphs: Children in care in Coventry live with carers approved by Coventry City Council's own fostering service or by independent agencies such as the services shown above. The council's plan for housing the children in its care, Homes for Children and Young People in Coventry 2023-27, counted 724 children looked after on 31 March 2023, about 1% of the city's children, and a higher rate per 10,000 children than England as a whole.

Most of those children live in foster homes, and in March 2023 about three in four of the children in foster care were with Coventry's own carers. The council had aimed for 285 children living with its own mainstream carers by then, reached 266, and says plainly that its targets have not been met. It wants more foster homes inside the city or within easy reach of children's schools, and it asks agencies for more local places too, so that children can stay near their school, friends and family.

Coventry says it particularly needs carers who can keep brothers and sisters together, carers for teenagers, and carers for children with more complex needs; its strategy also reports a widening gap in skilled carers for disabled children. It is especially looking for parent and child carers, and for its Next Steps scheme, a one-to-one therapeutic placement that asks for at least two years' experience of caring for or working with young people whose behaviour is challenging. To encourage people to take siblings, the council pays its fee for each child cared for.

The council's 2026/2027 payments leaflet sets a weekly allowance for each child from £195.67 for children up to 4 to £337.40 for young people aged 16 and over. Mainstream carers also receive a weekly fee per child of £175.40 at the standard level or £269.78 at the enhanced level, and five extra weeks of allowance are paid through the year for birthdays, festivals, holidays and clothing. Our Coventry allowance page has the full table.

Fostering with the council means joining the team at One Friargate that looks after the city's own children, and it runs drop-ins and information events. An agency approves, trains and supports you itself, and councils, Coventry among them, ask it to care for children who need a home. Speak to the council and two or three of the services above before you choose. If you live outside the city, see our pages for Warwickshire, Solihull, Birmingham and the West Midlands.
